common_name: Desert Icicle Daylily (2012 Lambert/Webster Unusual-Form Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions with the crown about an inch below soil level in full sun and well-drained soil, and expect the pinched, twisting segments typical of unusual-form daylilies rather than a flat, standard-form flower.

directions: Desert Icicle won the American Hemerocallis Society's Lambert/Webster Award in 2012, an honor given annually to the best unusual-form daylily judged on crispate, cascading, or spatulate floral segments. Grow it in full sun with consistent moisture during the growing season to support the narrow, twisting petals that distinguish unusual-form cultivars from standard daylilies. Divide crowded clumps every three to four years in early spring to keep bloom production strong.
sources: American Hemerocallis Society — Lambert/Webster Award winners list (daylilies.org)

common_name: Brer Rabbit's Baby Daylily (2010 Lambert/Webster Unusual-Form Daylily)

planting.note: Set divisions in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil; unusual-form daylilies like this one carry narrow, curled, or quilled segments rather than broad flat petals.

directions: Brer Rabbit's Baby earned the American Hemerocallis Society's Lambert/Webster Award in 2010, the national prize for the year's top unusual-form daylily. As with other cultivars in this class, expect twisting, spatulate, or cascading petal segments rather than the broad flat form of standard daylilies, giving the flower a distinctive spidery or ruffled look. Plant in full sun and divide every few years once clumps become crowded to sustain vigorous flowering.
sources: American Hemerocallis Society — Lambert/Webster Award winners list (daylilies.org)

common_name: Lola Branham Daylily (2003 Lambert/Webster Unusual-Form Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in full sun with the crown just below soil level; this unusual-form cultivar was recognized nationally for its distinctive segment shape rather than a standard flat bloom.

directions: Lola Branham took the American Hemerocallis Society's Lambert/Webster Award in 2003, the society's annual recognition for the best unusual-form daylily registered with crispate, cascading, or spatulate petal segments. Give it full sun and evenly moist, well-drained soil through the bloom season to encourage the heaviest flower production. Lift and divide congested clumps in early spring every three to four years to keep the planting vigorous.
sources: American Hemerocallis Society — Lambert/Webster Award winners list (daylilies.org)

common_name: Blueberry Cream Cupcake Daylily (2026 Georgia Doubles Appreciation Award)

planting.note: Plant divisions in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil; deadhead spent double blooms promptly since the extra layers of petals hold moisture and can rot in humid or rainy weather.

directions: Blueberry Cream Cupcake won the American Hemerocallis Society's Georgia Doubles Appreciation Award for 2026, the society's yearly recognition for the top double-flowered daylily cultivar. Double daylilies carry extra whorls of petaloid segments inside the normal bloom, giving a fuller, peony-like flower that benefits from regular deadheading in wet climates. Grow it in full sun with consistent moisture and divide crowded clumps every three to four years to maintain strong bloom counts.
sources: American Hemerocallis Society — Georgia Doubles Appreciation Award winners list (daylilies.org)

common_name: Pursuit of Pleasure Daylily (Georgia Doubles Appreciation Award Winner)

planting.note: Plant divisions in full sun in well-drained soil; this double-form cultivar has proven popular enough with voters to top the Georgia Doubles Appreciation Award ballot in more than one year.

directions: Pursuit of Pleasure, hybridized by David Kirchhoff, won the American Hemerocallis Society's Georgia Doubles Appreciation Award in both 2011 and again in 2025, a rare repeat showing for this annual best-double-daylily honor. Its fully double form carries extra rows of petaloid segments that benefit from deadheading after rain to prevent the dense flower from rotting. Grow it in full sun with regular moisture and divide established clumps every few years to keep bloom quality high.
sources: American Hemerocallis Society — Georgia Doubles Appreciation Award winners list (daylilies.org)

As a 'Topguns' series cultivar, it joins a well-regarded line of double daylilies bred for extra petal substance and consistent form. Plant in full sun with even moisture and divide congested clumps every three to four years to keep flowering strong.

directions: Libby Gallion, hybridized by Dale Hensley, won the American Hemerocallis Society's Georgia Doubles Appreciation Award in 2023 for the year's outstanding double daylily. The cultivar's fully double bloom form sets it apart from standard daylilies by carrying additional whorls of petaloid tissue within each flower. Give it full sun, consistent moisture, and periodic division every three to four years to keep the clump blooming heavily.

common_name: Queen's Nurse Clematis (Evison 2026 Chelsea Launch)

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring with roots kept cool and shaded, training stems onto a trellis or obelisk in full sun.

directions: Queen's Nurse was launched by Raymond Evison at the 2026 RHS Chelsea Flower Show to mark the partnership between the National Garden Scheme and the Queen's Institute of Community Nursing. As a late large-flowered Group 3 clematis, fresh growth produces paler, pink-striped blooms while older stems carry deeper solid-pink flowers later in the season. Train it up a trellis, obelisk, or through a shrub with its roots shaded and cut all growth back hard to about a foot above ground each late winter, since flowers form only on the current year's stems.
sources: Raymond Evison Clematis — official 2026 Chelsea launch announcement
National Garden Scheme (ngs.org.uk)

common_name: Eliza Clematis (Evison 2026 Chelsea Launch)

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring with roots shaded and cool, training new growth onto a trellis or obelisk in full sun.

directions: Eliza debuted alongside two sister cultivars at the 2026 RHS Chelsea Flower Show from Raymond Evison's breeding program. Its ruffled blooms open a soft violet-blue and mature to near-white, with deep red-tipped anthers providing contrast from late spring through early summer, with a repeat flush later in the season. As with other large-flowered Group 3 hybrids, prune it back hard each late winter to keep growth compact and flowering heavy on a trellis or obelisk in full sun.
sources: Raymond Evison Clematis — official 2026 Chelsea launch announcement

common_name: Ithemba Clematis (Evison 2026 Chelsea Launch)

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring with roots shaded and cool, training stems up a trellis or obelisk in full sun.

directions: Ithemba, whose name means 'hope' in Zulu, was previewed in Cape Town in October 2025 in partnership with a children's hospital charity and formally launched at the 2026 RHS Chelsea Flower Show as part of Raymond Evison's breeding program. Its ruffled white blooms are brushed with a pink bar and set off by striking red filaments and anthers, flowering from late spring into early summer with a second flush in late summer. Give it full sun on a trellis or obelisk with shaded roots, and prune hard in late winter as it blooms entirely on new growth.
sources: Raymond Evison Clematis — official 2026 Chelsea launch announcement
The Gardener (South Africa)
